html:
The French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon was French rule over the lands that became Syria and Lebanon, from 1920 to 1946, under a mandate of the League of Nations. The map shows it from 1920 to 1938.

After the Ottoman defeat, Faisal, leader of the Arab Revolt, was proclaimed king of an independent Syria in 1920. But under the Sykes-Picot Agreement Britain had promised Syria to France. French troops beat Faisal's small army at Maysalun in July 1920 and took Damascus.

France ruled by dividing. It created Greater Lebanon, with a Christian majority, and split Syria into separate states for Damascus, Aleppo, the Alawites and the Druze. The Great Syrian Revolt of 1925 to 1927 began among the Druze and spread; France shelled Damascus to crush it. In 1939 France handed the district of Alexandretta (Hatay) to Turkey. Syria and Lebanon won independence during and after the Second World War, and the last French troops left in 1946.
